source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Numbers 31–36 align directly with all 228 corresponding Hebrew records. Each original XML record is hashed in full. Earlier Numbers numbering differences and the two-record binding at public 26:1 remain preserved in earlier ledgers.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves Israel’s vengeance and the death idiom without replacing either with an explanation.
Keeps the shift from Israel’s vengeance to the LORD’s vengeance in Moses’ address.
Identifies Phinehas clearly but does not specify unmentioned holy articles.
Retains the unrestricted male terminology within this battle report rather than narrowing it to soldiers.
Makes captivity explicit and keeps children within the captured population.
Preserves Moses’ accusatory question and its broad category rather than softening the demand.
Attributes the accusation and Balaam connection to Moses’ speech here.
States the commanded killing of children and sexually experienced women explicitly.
Preserves both survival and the possessive captivity formula without adding an unrecorded fate.
Preserves the additional water requirement for fire-resistant objects, not an either-or substitution.
Retains the one-in-five-hundred levy and its application to people as well as animals.
Distinguishes the community’s one-in-fifty levy and its Levitical recipients.
Keeps 32000 human captives and the text’s sexual-experience classification explicit.
Retains the explicit allocation of thirty-two people as tribute.
Keeps the community’s human captives within the distribution rather than reducing the list to goods.
Presents the no-loss report as the officers’ own statement.
Retains atonement for lives and the five ornament categories, with lexical uncertainty noted in the apparatus.
